definitions.explanation: The sound made by clicking the tongue against the roof of the mouth, expressing irritation, annoyance, or displeasure. Considered rude in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{舌打|したう}ちをした。
{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}り{遅|おく}れて、{思|おも}わず{舌打|したう}ちした。
examples.english: I missed the train and couldn't help but click my tongue in frustration.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}の{前|まえ}で{舌打|したう}ちするのは{絶対|ぜったい}にやめたほうがいい。
examples.english: You should absolutely avoid clicking your tongue in front of your boss.

notes:
A compound of {舌|した} (tongue) and {打|う}ち (striking, from {打|う}つ). Used with する to form a verb: {舌打|したう}ちする.

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, {舌打|したう}ち is considered very rude and aggressive. Even doing it unconsciously can offend people nearby. It signals open displeasure and is associated with ill temper.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {舌打|したう}ちをする (to click one's tongue)
- {思|おも}わず{舌打|したう}ちする (to involuntarily click one's tongue)
- {小|ちい}さく{舌打|したう}ちする (to click one's tongue quietly)
